subject: Post-call: NeuroVista dedicated inference — SLO + isolation checklist
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@neurovista.ai>, Michael Patel <mpatel@neurovista.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: NeuroVista dedicated inference — SLO + isolation checklist

Emma / Michael — thanks again for the chat earlier. Quick written recap so we have alignment and clear next steps. TL;DR: NeuroVista wants predictable inference economics for clinical screening workloads, tenant isolation for PHI, and a 99th %-ile latency target for short prompts.

Pain points we captured:
- Spiky inference load during triage windows (peaks ~x5 baseline) — current infra causes queueing.
- Regulatory requirement: PHI must be isolated and auditable (SOC2 + internal audit).
- Cost variability: unpredictable token spend when using bursty shared endpoints.

Goals (customer):
1) Dedicated GPU pool with explicit isolation for PHI pipelines (logical or physical — preference for dedicated tenancy).
2) Latency SLO: 99th %-ile <= 350ms for 16–64 token prompts, P95 <= 120ms.
3) Throughput target: sustain 60 concurrent short-request QPS during peak windows, baseline steady-state 10 QPS.
4) Clear procurement path and rolling canary before full cutover.

Redwood proposal (recap):
- Reserved pool: 8x A100-class GPUs initially, autoscale + burst buffer to 12 GPUs during scheduled peak windows.
- Isolation: single-tenant queueing + network-level VPC peering for the private control plane; option for physically dedicated hosts if required by audit (we documented both in the attached topology).
- Observability & audit: token-level traces, request IDs, and an audit log export we retain for 90 days by default (longer retention available).
- SLO commitments: target 99th <= 350ms on the reserved pool (subject to model selection and quantization profile); fallback policy to a lower-cost variant with graceful degradation.

Attachments sent: NeuroVista-SLA-proposal-v1.pdf, isolation-topology.svg, and your traffic sample (nv-traffic-profile-nov.csv) — see attachments.

Asks / next steps:
1) Please confirm the isolation requirement: logical (tenant isolation on shared hosts) vs physical (dedicated servers). If physical required, procurement lead time moves by ~3–4 weeks.
2) Confirm acceptance of the SLO band above or propose adjustments.
3) If okay, we’ll put an initial SOW + pricing (commit + burst) and send a DocuSign for approval.

Proposed timeline:
- By Fri 11/27: sign SOW to start environment provisioning week of 12/7
- Week of 12/7: early canary with a subset of traffic (ops runbook + playbook dry run)
- By 12/21: full cutover if canary meets SLOs and compliance checks

I’m looping Ben and Rishi on ops and pricing details. Happy to jump on a 30-min follow-up if you want to walk through the topology.

Thanks —
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

Attachment stubs: [NeuroVista-SLA-proposal-v1.pdf (34 KB)], [isolation-topology.svg (8 KB)], [nv-traffic-profile-nov.csv (12 KB)]

From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@neurovista.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Patel <mpatel@neurovista.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: NeuroVista dedicated inference — SLO + isolation checklist

Thanks Hannah — appreciate the clear summary. A couple clarifications from our side: 

1) Isolation: we need physical separation for the PHI-handling pipeline (audit insists on no multi-tenant CPU/GPU hosts for that lane). Logical isolation is acceptable for non-PHI workloads.

2) SLO numbers: 99th <= 350ms for 16–64 tokens is fine as a launch target. Can we see an RU-based failure budget example in the SOW? We want to understand remediation steps and credit calculations.

3) Throughput: the 60 concurrent short-request QPS is what we see during triage windows. We will send an updated traffic dump (larger sample) by EOD Thurs.

4) Procurement: Michael (cc’d) will coordinate PO and our security questionnaire. Michael, please flag any gating items we need to surface to Redwood.

If Redwood can confirm the incremental lead time for physical-dedicated hosts (+3–4 weeks), we’ll aim to sign the SOW by 11/27 and start provisioning in early Dec.

—Emma
Emma Jones
Head of Product Research | NeuroVista
emma.jones@neurovista.ai | +1 (212) 555-0199

Hannah — quick internal notes and suggested pricing lane to include in the SOW: 

- Hardware sizing: 8x A100 (reserved) + autoscale to 12x for scheduled peaks (we should propose an hourly burst rate and an included burst credit pool).
- Isolation delta: physical hosts for PHI lane adds ~$22k/month OPEX relative to logical isolation (estimate includes host reservation premium and additional networking). Call it out as a separate line item.
- SLO credit model: propose 5% monthly service credit for rolling 99th > SLA (sliding window) with a tiered credit (5% -> 10% -> 20%) depending on recurrence; ops runbook included as Appendix A.
- Ops: canary run with 10% traffic for 72 hours, with rollback plan and detailed incident response obligations.

I’ll draft a pricing appendix and a short runbook snippet for Hannah to attach to the SOW.

Ben
